chunks: Saad narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman, the freedman of Tirbal, from Ubayd ibn Zur'ah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) would pray in the mosque, and he would spit in front of him, to his right, to his left, and behind him, on the pebbles, and he would not cover it.'
ai.seo_question: What was the practice of spitting during prayer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical etiquette (adab) of Imam al-Baqir (AS) regarding cleanliness during prayer, specifically the method of disposing of saliva in the mosque. By spitting onto pebbles without covering it, he demonstrated a balance between ritual purity and the natural, unpretentious conduct expected of the Imams, distinguishing their practice from later rigidifications. This narration serves as a primary source for understanding the physical aspects of Salah in the early Shia tradition, emphasizing ease and hygiene.
